At 12 noon July 6, some 10 staff members 
of the Hongkew Branch of the Great Feople's Society 
were urgently called to a meeting in the office of 
the Society at 427 East Seward Road when Waung Ming 
Sing ( 2} 4% Hy ), Chief of the Hongkew Branch, 
presided. He informed the attendance that 
instructions had been received from the Head Office 
of the Great People's Society in Nanking in which 
the various branches of the society were ordered 
to do their best in carrying out an anti-British 
propaganda campaign on July 7, the anniversary of 
the Lukouchiao Incident. A discussion then took 
Place and it was decided that because of the short 
motice given no preparations could be made and also 
as no funds had been received or issued for the 
carrying out of the campaign, nothing could be done 
on July 7. 

It is also learnec that the Head Office 
of the Great People's Society plans to conduct in 
the very near future an anti-British and anti- 
American propaganda campaign on a large scale.

REPORT
Date July 23, 1940.

Subject Anti-British and Anti-American campaign by Japanese sponsored
organizations.

Made by C.D.I. Kub Pao Hwa Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

（右上角印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY File No. D. 8252 (C)）

In connection with the attached report, it
has been found that instructions for an anti-British
campaign were also issued to other Japanese sponsored
organizations including the Chinese Labourers'
Welfare Association, who have now, it is learned,
been instructed by the Japanese Military Authorities
to cancel the orders received, **〔此处转录不清〕** LING TSE CHUN (Formosan),
Secretary of the Chinese Labourers' Welfare
Association, with offices at 20 Canton Road, has now
been given instructions for a new movement in
propaganda against the local American Defence Force
and has enlisted the support of a few other Japanese
sponsored organizations. A movement is now in
progress along the following lines :-
1) To launch an anti-American campaign and to intensify
anti-American propaganda.
2) To gather information on the various billets of
the American Defence Force re particulars of
armaments, etc.
3) To report to the Japanese Military Special Service
Section the usual haunts of amusement of the local
American marines, so as to enable the Japanese
Military Special Service agents to create an
incident as a retaliatory measure.

Referring to the report dated July 7, 1940

报告
日期：1940年7月23日。

主题：日本扶持的组织开展的反英、反美运动。

撰写人：侦探员 顾宝华（Kub Pao Hwa） 转呈人：督察长 克劳福德（Crawford）

（右上角印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处档案室 档案号 D. 8252 (C)）

关于随附的报告，经查发现，反英运动的指令也已下达给其他日本扶持的组织，包括中国劳工福利协会。据悉，该协会现已接到日本军方当局的指示，取消此前收到的命令，**〔此处转录不清〕** 中国劳工福利协会秘书林泽春（LING TSE CHUN，台湾人），办公地点位于广东路20号，现已接到关于开展针对当地美国防卫部队的新宣传运动的指令，并争取到了其他几个日本扶持组织的支持。目前正按以下方针开展运动：
1) 发起反美运动，加强反美宣传。
2) 收集有关美国防卫部队各处驻地的情报，包括武器装备详情等。
3) 向日本军方特务机关报告当地美国海军陆战队员常去的娱乐场所，以便日本军方特务人员制造事件，作为报复措施。

关于1940年7月7日的报告，大同社虹口分社社长汪銘新（Waung Ming Sing）前往南京

Subject Hongkew Branch of the Great People's Society - receives
instructions to carry out anti-British propaganda.

Made by D. I. Kao Yen-ken. Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

Comm.
No.
〔此处转录不清：左侧栏手写签名及日期戳记〕
〔印：POLICE 8 JULY 1940 COMMANDO〕

At 12 noon July 6, some 10 staff members
of the Hongkew Branch of the Great People's Society
were urgently called to a meeting in the office of
the Society at 427 East Seward Road when Waung Ming
Sing ( 汪銘新 ), Chief of the Hongkew Branch,
presided. He informed the attendance that
instructions had been received from the Head Office
of the Great People's Society in Nanking in which
the various branches of the society were ordered
to do their best in carrying out an anti-British
propaganda campaign on July 7, the anniversary of
the Lukouchiao Incident. A discussion then took
place and it was decided that because of the short
notice given no preparations could be made and also
as no funds had been received or issued for the
carrying out of the campaign, nothing could be done
on July 7.

It is also learned that the Head Office
of the Great People's Society plans to conduct in
the very near future an anti-British and anti-
American propaganda campaign on a large scale.

Kao Yen-ken
D. I.

D. C. ( Special Branch ).

Subject Officials of the Reformed Government not allowed to
join political parties
Made by/ ____ and ____ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang

I have been unable to obtain a copy of
the order referred to in attached report. It is
likely that verbal instructions may have been issued.
Tracing back to the orders of the Reformed
Government, the only instructions referring to the
prohibition of Government employees from joining
any political party appear to be the order mentioned
in Government Gazette No.20 of August 29, 1939.
It reads as follows :
"At the 41st meeting held by the Political
Affairs Committee of the Reformed Government of
the Chinese Republic on August 23, the following
resolution was discussed and passed :-
"'Government officials should always carry
out their duties in strict accordance with the
regulations governing their services. They are
not allowed to deviate from these regulations.
Ever since the Kuomintang came into power it has
plundered the people and brought extreme distress
upon the country because of its despotism so much
so that the country is now on the verge of its
annihilation. This should be a warning to us.
"'The object of the Reformed Government
of the Chinese Republic is to work for national
salvation and peace. Until the formal inauguration
of a proper and legitimate political party no
officials of this Government will be allowed to
join any party. Violation of this decision will

（批：Copy sent.）

S.I., Special Branch Station,
Date August 31 1939.

Subject. Great People Society - organization to be strengthened by
"Reformed Government."
Made by D.I. Pan Hien-pih, Forwarded by C. Coulson

The "Reformed Government" is endeavouring to
enlarge and strengthen the organization of the Great
People Society, and has appointed the following
officials to important posts in the society:-

Name and Office of Ref. Govt. official | Position in Great People Society
---|---
Liang Hung-tse (梁鴻志), President of Executive Yuan | Director-General.
Wen Tsung-yao (溫宗堯), President of Legislative Yuan | Deputy Director-General.
Chen Chun (陳群), Minister of Interior | Chairman.
Chu Ta-chwang (朱大璋), Member of Legislative Yuan | Chief of the Headquarters, Ranking.

The "Reformed Government" has also issued an
order instructing its employees to join the Great
People Society and forbids participation in any other
organizations.

The motive of this order and the proposed
development of the Great People Society would appear
to be a measure preventing "Reformed Government"
employees from joining the Wang Ching Wei clique thus
attempting to obstruct the influence of the "New
Kuomintang" which the Wang clique is attempting to
organize.

Pan Hien-pih
D. I.

A.C. (Special Branch).

Section 1, Special Branch A/99/6
Date Sept. 28, 1938.

Subject The Asia Rehabilitation Society - now known as Dah Ming Society (大民會).

Made by Dr. I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by C. Gaulton

The Asia Rehabilitation Society ("興亞會" Shing Yah Society) operated from an office in New Asia Hotel, Tiendong Road, the inauguration of the preparatory committee taking place on 22nd March 1935.

This Society first came to the notice of the Municipal Police in the middle of March 1938 when literature of an anti-Kuomintang and anti-Communist nature, came into our possession, the literature purporting to have emanated from the preparatory committee of this society. Other literature from the same source advocating the cultivation of friendship between the Japanese and Chinese people were also obtained.

With a view to organizing the Society on the lines of the Hsin Ming Hui of North China, it was proposed in April 1938 that the name be changed to that of the Shing Ya Tang (興亞黨) and one Wong Tsz-wei (王子惠) was put forward as head of the society, but for some unknown reason, those plans never took concrete shape.

Towards the end of June 1938 the name of the society was officially changed to the Dah Ming Society (大民會), but the administrative personnel remained the same. According to reports received this step was taken because of the nativity and unsavoury name the Asia Rehabilitation Society gained prevalent through corruption amongst its members.

The activities of the society following this procedure were insignificant, but two issues of a monthly magazine entitled the "New China" (新中國), which is definitely anti-Government and pro-Japanese in tone, appeared in July and August of this year and were published by the Publicity

主题：兴亚会——现称大民会（Dah Ming Society）。

撰写人：I. Kuh Pao-hwa 博士 转呈人：C. Gaulton

兴亚会（"興亞會" Shing Yah Society）在天潼路新亚酒店设有办事处，筹备委员会于1935年3月22日成立。

该社团首次引起工部局警务处注意是在1938年3月中旬，当时我们获取了据称出自该社团筹备委员会的反国民党、反共性质的宣传品。我们还获得了来自同一来源的其他宣传品，主张培养中日人民之间的友谊。

为了按照华北新民会的模式组织该社团，1938年4月曾提议将名称改为兴亚党（Shing Ya Tang），并推举王子惠（Wong Tsz-wei）为社团首领，但由于某些未知原因，这些计划从未具体落实。

1938年6月底，该社团名称正式更改为大民会（Dah Ming Society），但行政人员保持不变。根据收到的报告，采取这一步骤是因为兴亚会因其成员腐败而获得了不良名声和令人不快的名称。

此后该社团的活动微不足道，但今年7月和8月出版了两期月刊《新中国》（New China），其基调明确反政府、亲日，并由宣传部出版

Department of the Dah Ming Society, with offices at Lane

October 22, 1940. Morning Translation

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) publishes the following advertisement :-

GALA MEETING IN CELEBRATION OF THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE INAUGURATION OF THE SHANGHAI OFFICE OF THE GREAT PEOPLE'S ASSOCIATION OF CHINA

Date: 6 p.m. (Chinese time) October 23.
Venue: The Tairiku Guild Hall (大陸公會館), 288 Seward Road.
Programme: Modern drama by the Far Eastern Dramatic Group (遠東劇團) and popular Chinese and Japanese songs.
Sponsored by: The Shanghai Office of the Great People's Association of China.
Supported by: The "Sin Shun Pao."

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-

CONDITIONS IN NANTAO

Lest undesirable elements should mingle with the inhabitants in Nantao and with a view to preserving peace and good order in that area, the authorities at 8 a.m. yesterday instituted rigorous searches at the various iron gates along the border of Nantao and the French Concession and denied entry to all persons not in possession of citizens' certificates. It is learned that many people were turned away.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao of October 20 (editorial) :-

THE TRUTH ABOUT THE ITALO-GERMAN-JAPANESE ALLIANCE EXPOSED

When the Italo-German-Japanese Pact was signed, it was generally regarded as a plan of Germany to utilize Japan to harass the United States. Hitler had great hopes that Japan would intensify her southward advance so that collisions will break out between Japan on one side and the United States and Britain on the other, for such collisions would have embarrassed England and Hitler's attack on Britain would be facilitated. This was what Hitler had desired the most, for in that event the United States would have to concentrate her strength to deal with Japan and her assistance to Britain would have to be reduced. Hence, the press view throughout the world is that Germany was the promoter of the Italo-German-Japanese alliance; that Germany would benefit from the alliance in the future; that Japan would be misled and would also pay the greater price.

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）刊登如下广告：-

庆祝中华大民会上海办事处成立周年纪念盛大集会

地点：西华德路（Seward Road）288号大陆公会馆。
节目：远东剧团演出的现代戏剧及中日流行歌曲。

协办：《新顺报》。

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：-

南市情况

为防止不良分子混入南市居民之中，并为了维持该地区的和平与良好秩序，当局于昨日上午8时在南市与法租界边界沿线的各铁门实施了严格搜查，禁止所有未持有市民证的人员进入。据悉，许多人被拒之门外。

10月20日《华美晚报》社论：-

揭露意德日同盟之真相

当意德日协定签署时，普遍被视为德国利用日本骚扰美国的计划。希特勒曾寄予厚望，希望日本加强其南进政策，从而导致日本与美国及英国之间发生冲突，因为此类冲突将使英国陷入困境，并有利于希特勒对英国的攻击。这正是希特勒最期望看到的，因为在那种情况下，美国将不得不集中力量对付日本，从而减少其对英国的援助。因此，全球舆论认为德国是意德日同盟的推动者；德国将从该同盟中未来受益；日本将被误导，并将付出更大的代价。

现在，事实表明上述观点完全正确。德国与日本结盟仅仅是为了鼓励日本在远东制造麻烦，以便德国利用这一局势

October 22, 1940.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / 23 OCT. 1940 / COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）
Morning Translation

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald,
Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao :-

FRENCH TRAMWAY LABOUR DISPUTE SATISFACTORILY SETTLED

The labour dispute in the French Tramway
Company has lasted almost a month. Negotiations have been
going on between the two sides under the mediation of the
Political Branch of the French Police. At 5 p.m. yesterday,
further negotiations were held at the company's office on
Avenue Dubail with the result that a satisfactory settlement
was eventually reached. An agreement will be signed at
2 p.m. to-day. The tram and bus services in the French
Concession will be restored to-morrow.
Upon being notified by the Political Branch
of the French Police, the representatives of the workers and
the company attended further negotiations at the French
Tramway Company at 5 p.m. yesterday. Representatives of
the workers present were Zah Chuen-foh (石全福) and Chang
Foh-pao (张法宝) of the Mechanical Department and Pan
Loh-chi (潘乐志) and five others of the Traffic Department.
Chief of the Political Branch of the French Police and
Inspector Sih Keng-sun (施更生) were also present.
Representatives of the French Tramway Company were the
general manager and a compadore named Doo (杜). The
negotiations lasted one and a half hours and the strike was
settled. An agreement will be signed at 2 p.m. to-day.
The points considered during the negotiations
yesterday were (1) the reinstatement of the 46 workers who
were dismissed prior to the strike, and (2) increase of wages.
With regard to the first question, the company
promised to reinstate 30 of the men, instead of 26 as formerly
promised; the rest will be reinstated later. As for the
second question, the company promised to grant an increase
of $6 in the monthly allowance.
To-day the company will send out men to
inspect the tram tracks and wires and repair vehicles. The
strikers will resume work to-morrow.

Central China Daily News, Bing Pao, Kuo Min Daily News :-

The views of the two sides were brought closer
on October 20 after direct negotiations were held under the
mediation of the Political Branch of the French Police and
the Nanking People's Movement authorities. During the
negotiations on October 20 the company promised to reinstate
30 of the 45 workers dismissed by the company for organizing
a labour union, whilst the rest were to be reinstated later,
but the workers insisted that all the 45 dismissed men be
reinstated.
At 9 a.m. yesterday, further negotiations
were held at the company. Both sides were willing to make
concessions over the question of the reinstatement of the
dismissed workers. Hence, all conditions were eventually
settled. The negotiations lasted until 6 p.m. The
agreement will be published after it has been signed to-day.
It is expected that the strikers will resume work to-morrow.

P. T. O.

1940年10月22日。
（印：上海公共租界工部局 / 1940年10月23日 / 总监办公室）
晨间译稿

《正言报》、《中美日报》、《国民新闻》、
《申报》、《新晚报》：-

法商电车公司劳资纠纷圆满解决

法商电车公司的劳资纠纷已持续近一个月。双方在法租界警务处政治部的调解下进行了谈判。昨日下午5时，双方在杜美路（Avenue Dubail）的公司办公室举行了进一步谈判，最终达成了令人满意的解决方案。协议将于今日下午2时签署。法租界的电车和公共汽车服务将于明日恢复。
接到法租界警务处政治部的通知后，工人代表和公司代表于昨日下午5时在法商电车公司参加了进一步谈判。出席的工人代表有机务部的石全福和张法宝，以及车务部的潘乐志等五人。法租界警务处政治部主任和巡官施更生也出席了会议。法商电车公司的代表为总经理和一名姓杜的买办。谈判持续了一个半小时，罢工得以解决。协议将于今日下午2时签署。
昨日谈判中审议的问题包括：(1) 复职在罢工前被解雇的46名工人，以及 (2) 增加工资。关于第一个问题，公司承诺复职30人，而非此前承诺的26人；其余人员将在稍后复职。关于第二个问题，公司承诺每月津贴增加6元。
今日公司将派人检查电车轨道和电线，并维修车辆。罢工工人将于明日复工。

《华中日报》、《晶报》、《国民日报》：-

在法租界警务处政治部和南京民众运动当局的调解下进行直接谈判后，双方观点于10月20日趋于接近。在10月20日的谈判中，公司承诺复职因组织工会而被公司解雇的45名工人中的30人，其余人员将在稍后复职，但工人坚持要求全部复职这45名被解雇人员。
昨日上午9时，在公司举行了进一步谈判。双方均愿意在被解雇工人复职问题上做出让步。因此，所有条件最终得以解决。谈判持续至下午6时。协议将于今日签署后公布。预计罢工工人将于明日复工。

请续后页。
